root_cause.text: f2fs_put_super() did not wait for in-flight node page reads to complete before validating that all page reference counts are zero, leading to a false positive BUG_ON during unmount when pending reads increment the count after the check.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "it is possible that f2fs_put_super() is called before all node page reads are completed" and that "Adding a call to f2fs_wait_on_all_pages() for F2FS_RD_NODE fixes the problem." The patch moves the reference count check to after the cleanup of meta and node pages, but the critical addition of the wait call is described as necessary to ensure reads complete. The original code at fs/f2fs/super.c:1939 (the BUG location) triggered because the count check occurred while asynchronous node page reads were still outstanding.

candidates.rationale: This truncation of the meta mapping may occur before pending node page reads complete; after truncation, in-flight reads increment page reference counts, making the later reference count check fail.
This loop iterates over all page count types, including node pages, without first waiting for pending reads; thus, pending reads can cause non-zero counts that trigger false BUG_ON.
This condition checks if the page count is zero; if pending node page reads have incremented the count after a previous truncation, the check will fail and incorrectly indicate a leak.

This BUG_ON is triggered when a non-zero page count is detected; since no wait for in-flight node page reads occurred before this check, a transient count due to pending reads causes a false positive crash during unmount.
This additional BUG_ON checks fsync node count, which could also be non-zero due to pending node page operations that have not completed, contributing to a false positive unmount BUG.
